newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: HOLD Paraguay gold prospecting leads to large find.
newsitem.headline: HOLD Paraguay gold prospecting leads to large find.

text.p: Gold prospecting by a U.S. firm in Paraguay has led to a find of a considerable concentration of the precious metal, official sources said Monday.

"Prospecting carried out by the firm Yamana Resources Inc has led to a find of a gold concentration of a little more than three percent in the areas extracted," Agustin Lopez Nunez, director of mineral resources at the Public Works Ministry, told Reuters.

Concessions by Paraguay to firms like Yamana for prospecting are granted for one year at a time. Concessions for exploration and extraction of study material are for two year periods and the concessions for actual mining are for 25 years. The mining concessions are renewable.
Paraguay's mining laws allow each firm to prospect in areas no larger than 50,000 hectares. The state will retain five percent of all minerals extracted.

However, President Juan Wasmosy has proposed lowering the portion kept by the state to 2.5 percent, enlarging the area allowed to one company to 150,000 hectares and lifting all import duties on machinery to be used in the mine.
